proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a regular conditional law given \(E_0\), and write
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
All constants below are chosen inside the nonempty interior of the fixed support, variance, Holder, covariance, and modulus envelopes.  The query is placed in a fixed compact subset of the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\), contained in \(\mathcal Z_+\).  Event outcomes are drawn independently of \(\mathscr X\), and, conditional on \(\mathscr X\), historical errors are drawn independently across units with conditional mean zero.  Thus
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{1}
\]
Unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes are completed so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Setting observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, and making every potential outcome independent of other units' assignments, verifies consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and event transport.  Bounded Bernoulli response kernels with probabilities in a fixed compact subset of \((0,1)\) verify boundedness and the conditional-variance lower bound.  The donor sample is conditionally iid, independent of the panel, with covariance in the declared ellipticity interval and standardized fourth moment within its envelope.  Finally set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Hence every experiment constructed below is a regular conditional law in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and (1) verifies the two additional full-design restrictions directly.

We first record an elementary binary divergence bound.  If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), Taylor's formula for
\(x\mapsto x\log(x/p)+(1-x)\log\{(1-x)/(1-p)\}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le \frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{2}
\]
Conditional independence makes the divergence of the response product the sum of the conditional binary divergences.

For the treated channel put \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and change the event Bernoulli mean in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Because \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge \pi_s^2/n_s\), one has \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\), so all probabilities remain in the fixed interior interval along the stated arrays.  The target separation is
\[
\sum_s\pi_sv_s
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{-1/2}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\tag{3}
\]
whereas (2) bounds the joint divergence by
\[
C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{4}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and set
\[
b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
For a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump \(\psi\) with \(\psi(0)=1\), perturb only cohort \(s_*\) by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{5}
\]
Take \(c_1\) small enough to preserve the response interior, the Holder radius, and the two-sided local modulus.  For \(\lambda>1\) use a common affine carrier with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient; for \(0<\lambda\le1\) use a common asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier.  The perturbation is small in the relevant Holder norm, so the carrier's lower modulus remains bounded away from zero.  Since \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\left|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)\right|^2
=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The perturbation is supported on a set of design probability at most \(Cb^d\).  Integrating (2) over the design and summing over the \(Tn_{s_*}\) responses gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{7}
\]

For the spacing channel use the pair in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  Its construction obeys (1), all one-time density bounds, and the frozen geometric mixing envelope; its observed laws coincide on the no-active-block event of probability at least a fixed positive constant.  Its squared target separation is at least
\[
c\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus this pair has positive testing affinity.  No bounded Kullback--Leibler assertion is made for it.

For the donor channel retain the affine carrier when \(\lambda>1\) and the asymmetric cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  By the lower half of the local-modulus condition, for \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\le\delta_0\) there is an admissible direction \(u_N\), or a direction attaining half the supremum, such that
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2\le c_2N^{-1/2},
\qquad
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose a fixed common-support finite-dimensional donor submodel whose probability vector is tilted by order \(N^{-1/2}\) in the direction \(\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\).  The tilt can be chosen inside the covariance and fourth-moment envelopes; its score is bounded and has nonsingular information.  A direct Taylor expansion of the finite probability-vector likelihood gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete the untreated event potential outcomes under each law with means \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (9) into the target separation, whose square is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

It remains only to translate (4), (7), and (10) into affinity.  For any two laws let \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), \(p=P_1(A)\), and \(q=P_0(A)\).  Applying Jensen's inequality separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\), and differentiating the resulting binary divergence twice, yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
\ge2(p-q)^2.
\]
Since \(p-q=\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (11) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and donor pairs; (8) supplies affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (2) verify membership in the full-design-centered class for all four pairs, which proves the claim.

For a channel \(q\), let \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) be the pair supplied by \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, let its two target values be \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  The pair has affinity at least \(a_0>0\) and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\), where the spacing component of \(R_q\) is \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  For every estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E_0'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E_1'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Consequently
\[
P_{0,q}(E_0')+P_{1,q}(E_1')
\ge\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge \frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}
\ge cR_q.
\tag{12}
\]
Taking the maximum over the four channels, then the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and finally the infimum over estimators proves the lower bound \(cR_{\star,\beta}\).

For the upper bound, condition on \(\mathscr X\), \(E_0\), and the donor sample.  By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the estimation error on a successful fit is the sum of four terms:
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{13}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}
=\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}
=\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\(B_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is the Taylor remainder, and \(B_{\mathrm{don}}\) is the difference between the weighted regression surface at the fold centers and at \(z_0\).

The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums conditional on the displayed conditioning sigma-field.  Conditional cross-unit independence and boundedness therefore give
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\tag{14}
\]
and, using \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control},
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{15}
\]
No temporal independence inside a unit history is used in (15).

On the kernel support, \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2\le C_Kh_{sk}\).  The deterministic weight bound and the Taylor remainder therefore yield
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_k h_{sk}^{\lambda}.
\tag{16}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), use fixed \(S,K_D\), and apply Cauchy--Schwarz to (16).  On the good sample,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mid E_0]
\le C\left\{
R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}
\right\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{17}
\]
because \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}=R_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For a donor complement of size \(m_k\), independence and the fourth-moment calculation used in the honest-interval proof give
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left\{m_k^{-1}\sum_{j\notin k}Z_j-z_0\right\}
\right\|_2^4\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le Cm_k^{-2}.
\tag{18}
\]
Projection onto the cube and donor ellipticity change the right side only by a fixed constant.  On the event where the resulting norm is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local modulus bounds the squared fold discrepancy by a constant times that norm to power \(2\kappa\).  Lyapunov's inequality applied to (18) yields \(Cm_k^{-\kappa}\).  On its complement, boundedness of the surfaces and Markov's inequality applied to (18) give \(Cm_k^{-2}\).  Since the number of folds is fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{19}
\]

The raw fitted intercept is bounded on every successful fit by \(B\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2}\), while a failed intercept is defined as zero.  Thus the squared estimation error is uniformly bounded by a fixed constant on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability bound in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes its risk contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  Combining (13)--(19) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{20}
\]

For completeness, the smoothing term is never uniquely active.  With
\(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\), weighted arithmetic--geometric mean gives, cohort by cohort,
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
After weighting and summing,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}+T^{-2\lambda/d}
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Equations (12) and (20) establish the asserted same-class bracket in every relative-growth regime.  The covariance estimator is feasible by spectral clipping, but neither (18) nor the estimator requires the donor law to be homoskedastic or Gaussian.

Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  Polynomial reproduction on every successful fit gives
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{stik}p(u_{stk})=p(0)
\]
for every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(r\).  Apply this identity to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\).  The Holder remainder then gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk}
-m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
-\sum_{t,i}a_{stik}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{22}
\]
After weighting cohorts and averaging folds, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} gives conditional mean zero, and conditional cross-unit independence makes the \(U_{si}\) independent over \((s,i)\) under the displayed conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|.
\]
If a centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its conditional moment generating function by the endpoint mixture with the same mean; elementary one-variable differentiation of that mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\]
Multiplication over independent units, Chernoff's inequality, and optimization in \(v\) therefore give
\[
P\!\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{23}
\]

Similarly define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\right\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers these variables conditional on \((\mathscr X,E_0)\).  They are independent across units and have range lengths at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation gives
\[
P\!\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{24}
\]
No independence between a unit's event outcome and its historical path is invoked: (23) and (24) will be combined by Bonferroni.

For donor fold \(k\), put \(m=m_k\) and \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\).  Donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors with \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding the fourth power and retaining precisely the index patterns in which every centered vector occurs at least twice yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|m^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
&=m^{-1}\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1m\right)
\left\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\right\}\\
&\le \frac Bm+\left(1-\frac1m\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
\]
Markov's inequality at \(q_k\) gives conditional error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}/K_D\) for this fold.  Euclidean projection onto the closed cube is nonexpansive because, coordinate by coordinate, truncation to \([0,1]\) cannot increase distance from the point \(z_0\) already in the cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds then imply, on the calibrated event,
\[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left\{\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0\right\}
\right\|_2
\le \sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,\frac{q_k}{\sqrt{m_k}}
=\delta_k.
\tag{26}
\]
A union bound over folds has total error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\).  On the good sample \(\delta_k\le\delta_0\); hence the upper local-modulus inequality and (26) give
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_k^\kappa.
\tag{27}
\]
Averaging (27) over folds gives \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).

By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the error of the full-data raw estimator is the event fluctuation in (24), minus the historical fluctuation in (23), minus the Taylor remainder in (22), minus the generated-center discrepancy in (27).  Bonferroni and
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}+
\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha
\]
show that, on the good sample,
\[
P\{|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\le H_\alpha\mid E_0\}
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]
On the bad sample the interval is \([-B,B]\), and \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) by bounded event wealth.  Thus (28) proves the asserted uniform conditional coverage.  Notice that it uses neither studentization nor any lower conditional-variance assumption for event outcomes.

We next bound expected length.  The deterministic conclusion of \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\sqrt{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\sqrt{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}}.
\tag{29}
\]
The kernel support and the same weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_kh_{sk}^\lambda.
\]
The bandwidth moment in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control}, now with exponent \(\lambda\), implies
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{30}
\]
Because \(D,S,K_D\) are fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\), (25) makes \(q_k\) uniformly bounded, whence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}
=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{31}
\]
By the selector-control lemma, the bad-sample probability is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  The fallback interval has length at most \(2B\), and \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\) eventually.  Equations (29)--(31), together with \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on the good sample, prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{32}
\]

For the matching lower bound, reduce the fixed perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so that every channel affinity \(A_q\) is greater than \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\).  This is also possible for the rare-block pair by reducing its active-block intensity while retaining a fixed positive separation constant.  Let \(I\) be uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge \mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
On the event in (33), \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge\Delta_q\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0\Delta_q
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\]
Maximizing over the four channels gives the lower bound
\(c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Together with (28) and (32), this proves the same-class expected-length bracket in every relative-growth regime.

added_lemmas.statement:
On every successful normalized-shape fit,
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{stik}|
\le\{L_{sk}e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}
\le c_G^{-1/2}.
\]
Because the weights and covariates do not depend on the replicated-unit index,
\[
\sum_t|a_{stik}|\le\frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s},
\qquad
\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\le\frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s},
\]
and hence
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
The exact Taylor bias is bounded by \(A_L\).  These conclusions are deterministic on successful fits and require no upper local-mass event.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Suppress \((s,k)\), write \(\mathsf L=L_{sk}\), \(G=G_{sk}\), and set
\(v_{ti}=w_{stk}^{1/2}b_r(u_{stk})\).  Then
\[
G=\sum_{t,i}v_{ti}v_{ti}^\top,
\qquad
a_{stik}=w_{stk}^{1/2}e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
&\le
\left\{\sum_{t,i}(e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\{e_0^\top G^{-1}GG^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}\mathsf L^{1/2}
=\{\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The selector requires \(G/\mathsf L\succeq c_GI\), so
\(G^{-1}\preceq(c_G\mathsf L)^{-1}I\).  Under the declared monomial normalization \(e_0=b_r(0)\) is the constant-monomial coordinate and \(\|e_0\|_2=1\).  Hence
\[
\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\le c_G^{-1}.
\]
For fixed \((s,t,k)\), neither \(u_{stk}\) nor \(w_{stk}\) depends on \(i\), whereas
\[
G=n_s\sum_tw_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^\top.
\]
Thus \(a_{stik}\) is constant in \(i\), and
\[
n_s\sum_t|a_{stik}|=\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
\le c_G^{-1/2}.
\]
The triangle inequality after averaging the fixed donor folds gives the same bound for \(\bar a_{sti}\).  Therefore
\[
\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le\sum_sn_s\left(\frac{\pi_sc_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}\right)^2
=c_G^{-1}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
Finally, the normal equations reproduce every polynomial of total degree at most \(r\).  Subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\), applying
\[
|m_s(x)-T_{r,\widetilde z_{sk}}m_s(x)|
\le C_{r,d}L\|x-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
and summing the absolute weighted remainders gives exactly \(A_L\).  No upper bound on \(L_{sk}\) was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(h_{sk}\) be selected by the normalized-shape rule in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  For a sufficiently large fixed initial-scale constant and some fixed \(A>2\lambda/d+2\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), every donor fold, every cohort, and every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_{s,\beta}\le1\),
\[
P\{h_{sk}>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A}.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}]
\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}
+\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}
+N^{-a/2}\right\}.
\]
The terminal-grid failure probability is at most
\(C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}\), and the total bad-sample probability in \texttt{def:honest-interval} is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the stated arrays.  These bounds allow \(Th_{s,\beta}^d=O(1)\) and impose no upper local-count event.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Condition on \((E_0,\widetilde z_{sk})\).  Donor independence implies that the conditional law and beta-mixing envelope of the historical design are unchanged.  For a candidate center \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and bandwidth \(h\), define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
The kernel is nonnegative, bounded, compactly supported, and positive on a neighborhood of zero.  The design density is between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\), and the dimension and polynomial degree are fixed.  A change of variables, with the one-sided truncation allowed at a cube boundary, therefore gives constants \(c_0,C_0>0\) such that, uniformly in \(z\), \(h\in(0,1]\), and unit vectors \(v\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\),
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d,
\qquad
\mathbb E[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]\ge c_0h^d.
\tag{34}
\]
The last inequality holds because a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on a set with nonempty interior; compactness of the unit sphere, of the cube, and of \([0,1]\) after rescaling makes the lower bound uniform.  Choose \(c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Put \(b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil\), where \(C_\beta\) is large enough that
\[
T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A}.
\tag{35}
\]
Partition the calendar indices into consecutive blocks of length \(b_T\), and separate them into odd and even block families.  Blocks of a fixed parity are separated by at least \(b_T\) indices.  By the definition of absolute regularity, the joint law of one new block and the preceding blocks differs in total variation from the product of its marginal law and the preceding joint law by at most \(\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\).  The overlap measure explicitly couples these two laws with mismatch probability equal to that total variation.  Induction over blocks consequently couples each parity family to independent blocks with total mismatch probability at most \(CT\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}/b_T\le CT^{-A}\).

For either parity and any one of the bounded nonnegative scalar functions \(F=\ell_{z,h}\) or \(F=v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\), let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) in block \(g\).  Then \(0\le W_g\le Cb_T\), and
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
\le Cb_T\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g]
\le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{36}
\]
For independent coupled blocks, the exponential-moment argument obtained by expanding \(e^{u(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)}\), bounding all terms of order at least two by the range in (36), and optimizing \(u\), gives
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_g(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)\right|>cTh^d
\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{37}
\]
Adding the coupling error in (35) gives the same inequality plus \(CT^{-A}\) for the original blocks.

Apply (37) to the local mass and, for the matrix lower bound, to a fixed finite \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  Since \(q_r\) is fixed, the net cardinality is fixed.  The usual net inequality follows directly by choosing a net point within distance \(1/4\) of an eigenvector and using the uniform boundedness of \(b_r\) on the kernel support.  Equations (34)--(37), applied to both block parities and then added, imply
\[
P\left\{L_{sk}(h)=0\ \text{or}\
\lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{G_{sk}(h)}{L_{sk}(h)}\right)<c_G
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A}.
\tag{38}
\]
Replicated rows multiply both \(G_{sk}(h)\) and \(L_{sk}(h)\) by \(n_s\), so they do not change the normalized shape event.

By definition of \(h_{s,\beta}\) and the sufficiently large constant \(C_h\),
\[
\frac{T(2^vh_{s,\beta})^d}{b_T}\ge c2^{vd}.
\]
If the selector has not stopped by \(2^vh_{s,\beta}\), that candidate fails; (38) therefore proves the displayed tail bound.  At \(h=1\), (38) gives terminal failure probability at most
\[
C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}.
\tag{39}
\]

For the moment bound, use the dyadic tail sum
\[
\mathbb E[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}]
\le h_{s,\beta}^a
+\sum_{v:2^vh_{s,\beta}<1}
(2^{v+1}h_{s,\beta})^aP\{h_{sk}>2^vh_{s,\beta}\}.
\]
The series \(\sum_v2^{av}\exp(-c2^{vd})\) converges, while the contribution of \(T^{-A}\) is at most \(CT^{-A}\) because the dyadic values are capped at one.  The chosen \(A\), and the three terms defining \(h_{s,\beta}\), give the claimed moment inequality.

Finally, for fixed \(S,K_D\), a union bound in (39) controls every selected fit.  Donor complements are nonempty eventually; all weights and radii are finite on a successful fit; spectral clipping is a defined measurable operation for every finite sample covariance; and \(\max_k\delta_k\le\delta_0\) eventually because \(m_k\asymp N\).  Thus the total bad probability is bounded by the right side of (39), which is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every array.  This proves all assertions without declaring large local counts bad.

added_lemmas.statement:
For fixed \(d\) and \(\lambda\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,T},P_{1,T})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
with the declared marginal design-density bounds and geometric conditional beta-mixing envelope such that
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
The event means are stable given the complete historical design, the historical errors are centered given that design, and both laws satisfy the maintained two-sided local modulus.  Consequently the spacing contribution to conditional minimax MSE is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), and every uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest interval has worst-case expected length at least \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  Hence the logarithm in the uniform geometric-mixing spacing term is unavoidable without an additional anti-clustering restriction.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix an interior point \(z_0\) and a sufficiently small constant \(c_p>0\).  Let
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L>0\) is small enough that
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{40}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Such a fixed \(c_L\) exists because choosing \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\) makes \(\rho_0^{L_T}\) decay strictly more slowly than \(L_T/T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at \(z_0\), contained in the cube, with Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  Its radius satisfies
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{41}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently over blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the design points in block \(b\) independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  Since \(\operatorname{Leb}_d(A_T)=p_T\), every one-time marginal density is exactly one:
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the declared design-density bounds hold.

If two calendar sigma-fields are separated by at least \(L_T\), they depend on disjoint independent block variables and are independent.  At a smaller lag, only a shared block can induce dependence.  Conditional on the binary block state the two parts are independent, and direct expansion of the two-component mixture shows that its absolute-regularity distance from the corresponding product law is at most \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Hence, by (40),
\[
\beta_P(k\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le k<L_T,\\
0,&k\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^k.
\tag{43}
\]

Let \(g\) be a bounded Holder surface in the interior of the response range.  When \(\lambda>1\), choose \(g\) with a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\); when \(0<\lambda\le1\), choose an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there.  In either case its covariance-standardized local modulus lies strictly between the two maintained bounds after a fixed rescaling.  Let \(\psi\) be a smooth compactly supported bump in the unit ball with \(\psi(0)=1\), and define
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_0}{h_T}\right).
\tag{44}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_b>0\), both surfaces remain in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and in the bounded response interior.  For \(\lambda>1\), the perturbation changes increments by at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and by at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\); hence it cannot cancel the affine lower modulus.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), its increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so a small \(c_b\) cannot cancel the cusp lower modulus.  The Holder upper bound gives the upper modulus in both cases.  Thus both laws satisfy the maintained two-sided modulus with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Given the complete design, draw bounded response errors independently across units, centered conditional on that design, with conditional variance at least \(B^{-1}\), and set the historical response mean to \(m_\ell(X_{st})\) under law \(\ell\).  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of the design with the same mean under both laws.  Complete the untreated event potential outcomes with cohort-average mean \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  This verifies event transport, and it gives
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{45}
\]
All remaining cohorts, donors, and potential outcomes are held fixed under the two laws and completed inside the frozen envelopes.  Equations (42)--(45) verify membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  Since the number of blocks is \(T/L_T+O(1)\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}
\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{46}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), every design point lies outside \(A_T\), where the two surfaces in (44) agree.  The complete observed-data laws therefore coincide on this event, so
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{47}
\]
The observed event mean is common, while event transport changes the untreated event mean by \(m_1(z_0)-m_0(z_0)=c_bh_T^\lambda\).  In a fixed positive-weight cohort the identification formula therefore gives
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{48}
\]
The two-point squared-error argument applied to (47)--(48) gives the MSE lower bound.  Reducing \(c_p\) makes the affinity in (47) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\); integrating simultaneous coverage against the overlap measure, as in (33), gives the expected-length lower bound.  No sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering premise is used.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Split \((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) into a fixed number \(K_D\) of folds.  For fold \(k\), project the complementary donor mean onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\), and denote cohort \(s\)'s block by \(\widetilde z_{sk}\).  Let
\[
h_{s,\beta}
=1\wedge C_h\left[
(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}
\vee N^{-1/2}
\right],
\]
where \(C_h\) is a fixed sufficiently large procedural constant depending only on \(\beta_0,\rho_0,d,\lambda\) and the fixed design and kernel constants.  For a candidate dyadic bandwidth \(h\) from \(h_{s,\beta}\) through \(1\), set
\[
u_{stk}(h)=\frac{X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}}h,
\qquad
w_{stik}(h)=K(u_{stk}(h)),
\]
\[
L_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stik}(h),
\qquad
G_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{stik}(h)b_r(u_{stk}(h))b_r(u_{stk}(h))^\top.
\]
Select the first candidate satisfying
\[
L_{sk}(h)>0,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sk}(h)/L_{sk}(h)\}\ge c_G,
\]
where \(c_G>0\) is fixed and depends only on the fixed kernel, polynomial basis, design-density bounds, and cube geometry.  Failure means that no grid value through \(1\) passes; no upper local-mass condition is imposed.  On success, set \(h_{sk}=h\), \(u_{stk}=u_{stk}(h)\), \(w_{stk}=K(u_{stk})\), and let \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) minimize
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{stk}\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^\top\gamma\}^2.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat m_s=K_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk},
\qquad
\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\}.
\]
On a failed fold fit set its intercept contribution to zero.  Estimate \(\Sigma\) by the spectrally clipped full sample covariance \(\widehat\Sigma\); no clipping is applied to a successful fitted intercept or to \(\widehat\tau\).

\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}

\]
and the two bounded-summand radii

=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}

\[

=B\left\{

\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
For donor fold \(k\) with complementary size \(m_k\), put \(D=Sd\),
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
M_4(m_k)=\frac B{m_k}
+\left(1-\frac1{m_k}\right)(D^2+2D),

\[

\qquad

\qquad

\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\delta_k^\kappa.

\[

\qquad

proposed.name: Log-adjusted generated-center replicated local-polynomial estimator
proposed.construction:
Split \((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) into a fixed number \(K_D\) of folds.  For fold \(k\), project the complementary donor mean onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\), and denote cohort \(s\)'s block by \(\widetilde z_{sk}\).  Let
\[
h_{s,\beta}
=1\wedge C_h\left[
(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}
\vee N^{-1/2}
\right],
\]
where \(C_h\) is a fixed sufficiently large procedural constant depending only on \(\beta_0,\rho_0,d,\lambda\) and the fixed design and kernel constants.  For a candidate dyadic bandwidth \(h\) from \(h_{s,\beta}\) through \(1\), set
\[
u_{stk}(h)=\frac{X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}}h,
\qquad
w_{stik}(h)=K(u_{stk}(h)),
\]
\[
L_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stik}(h),
\qquad
G_{sk}(h)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{stik}(h)b_r(u_{stk}(h))b_r(u_{stk}(h))^\top.
\]
Select the first candidate satisfying
\[
L_{sk}(h)>0,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\{G_{sk}(h)/L_{sk}(h)\}\ge c_G,
\]
where \(c_G>0\) is fixed and depends only on the fixed kernel, polynomial basis, design-density bounds, and cube geometry.  Failure means that no grid value through \(1\) passes; no upper local-mass condition is imposed.  On success, set \(h_{sk}=h\), \(u_{stk}=u_{stk}(h)\), \(w_{stk}=K(u_{stk})\), and let \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) minimize
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{stk}\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^\top\gamma\}^2.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat m_s=K_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk},
\qquad
\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\}.
\]
On a failed fold fit set its intercept contribution to zero.  Estimate \(\Sigma\) by the spectrally clipped full sample covariance \(\widehat\Sigma\); no clipping is applied to a successful fitted intercept or to \(\widehat\tau\).

proposed.name: Full-data Hoeffding--Taylor--donor interval
proposed.construction:
Set
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}
=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/3.
\]
Use the full-data donor folds, projected complementary-fold centers, log-adjusted bandwidth grid, normalized-shape selection rule, and raw local-polynomial fits in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  On every successful fit define
\[
G_{sk}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^\top,
\qquad
a_{stik}=e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk}),
\]
\[
\bar a_{sti}=K_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}a_{stik},
\qquad
\widehat m_s=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\bar a_{sti}Q_{sti}.
\]
Define the exact Taylor allowance
\[
A_L=C_{r,d}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}
\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
|a_{stik}|\,\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
and the two bounded-summand radii
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\right\}^{1/2},
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
For donor fold \(k\) with complementary size \(m_k\), put \(D=Sd\),
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
M_4(m_k)=\frac B{m_k}
+\left(1-\frac1{m_k}\right)(D^2+2D),
\]
\[
q_k=\left\{\frac{K_DM_4(m_k)}{\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\right\}^{1/4},
\qquad
\delta_k=\sqrt{\frac{C_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}}\frac{q_k}{\sqrt{m_k}},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{don}}=\frac{C_{\mathrm{mod}}}{K_D}
\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\delta_k^\kappa.
\]
On the good sample set
\[
H_\alpha=R_{\mathrm{hist}}+R_{\mathrm{evt}}+A_L+A_{\mathrm{don}},
\qquad
C_\alpha=[-B,B]\cap
[\widehat\tau-H_\alpha,\widehat\tau+H_\alpha].
\]
The bad-sample event is the union of: an empty donor complement; failure of any selected Gram matrix under the normalized-shape rule; nonfiniteness of a required weight or radius; undefined spectral clipping; and \(\max_k\delta_k>\delta_0\).  On that event set \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
 \qquad
 q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
We first derive the scalar inequality used below.  For \(u>0\), let
\(\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a\).  Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
 \phi'(u)=a(1-u^{a-1}).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on
\((1,\infty)\).  Hence \(\phi(u)\geq 0\) for every \(u>0\).  Substitution of
\(u=x/y\), followed by multiplication by \(y>0\), gives
\[
 x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
 \qquad x,y>0.
\]
The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give \(q(1-a)=a\).  Therefore, for each
cohort \(s\), positivity of \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits the preceding inequality
with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\), yielding
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}
 \leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\]
Since \(T\geq1\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Thus the corrected
spacing definition in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} implies
\[
 T^{-q}
 \leq (\log2)^{-q}
 \left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
 =(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Multiplying the cohortwise bound by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), and using
\(\sum_s\pi_s^2\leq(\sum_s\pi_s)^2=1\), which follows from positivity and
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)T^{-q}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2\\
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
 &\leq C_{\lambda,d}
   \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq1.
\]
Let
\[
 A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
 \qquad
 D:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
The corrected frontier definition and the last display imply, equation by
equation,
\[
 D\leq R_{\star,\beta}
 =A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}D.
\]
This proves
\(R_{\star,\beta}\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), uniformly
in the positive sample sizes; the constants do not depend on \(N\), \(T\), or
\(\mathbf n\).

By \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\), whereas
\(A\) is independent of \(N\).  Consequently the donor contribution is
asymptotically negligible exactly in the oracle region
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates exactly in the generated-center region
\[
 A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
Equality up to positive constants, \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\), is equivalent,
because \(\kappa>0\), to
\[
 N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
These comparisons become minimax phases whenever a separate sharp-risk theorem
establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) for the experiment in question.

For the stricter independent-design or fixed-query comparator, retain
\(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\).  The same cohortwise inequality, without the
logarithmic comparison, gives
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
 \leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
The comparator definition of \(R_\star\) therefore yields the exact identity
\[
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} states
\(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Hence using the recorded historical
coordinate does not require inversion of a measurement-error convolution.
Inspection of \texttt{def:rate-frontier} then confirms that its bookkeeping has
no deconvolution component and no separately postulated moving-Gram rate.  This
is an algebraic and observation-structure conclusion, not an independent
sharpness claim.  Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\); thus \(\lambda>1\)
implies \(\kappa=1\), and the donor term is
\(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\), proving higher-smoothness saturation.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\) and all positive sample sizes, let
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
 +\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log2)^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
Then
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \qquad
 R_{\star,\beta}
 \asymp_{\lambda,d}
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently, in any experiment for which \(R_{\star,\beta}\) is established
as the sharp risk, the oracle region is
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\]
the generated-center region is
\[
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=o(N^{-\kappa}),
\]
and the boundary is
\[
 N\asymp
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Under a stricter independent-design or fixed-query condition that delivers the
comparator spacing term \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), one instead has
the exact relations
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
 \qquad
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} removes a classical
measurement-error inverse problem from the historical design; accordingly the
defined bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate
moving-Gram rate.  Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever
\(\lambda>1\).  These algebraic conclusions do not by themselves assert that
either frontier is sharp for a statistical experiment.

proposed.consumer: A study can allocate its data budget to the active axis and avoid unnecessary deconvolution when the historical paths are exact.
